                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

Unser Ziel ist es, bereits in der Bewerbungsphase für Kandidaten und Kunden die Grundlagen für eine positive und gesunde Zusammenarbeit zu schaffen.

„Personaldienstleistungsmanufaktur mit Herz“ (Kununu-Bewertung)

Aufgaben

  • Planung und Steuerung der präventiven Instandhaltung über alle technischen Anlagen zur Minimierung ungeplanter Ausfälle und Optimierung der Wartungszyklen.
  • Sicherstellung der Verfügbarkeit aller technischen Systeme (BMS, HVAC, Mittel-/Niederspannung, Sanitär, Brandschutz, Laborlüftung) entsprechend vertraglicher Vereinbarungen.
  • Führung und Entwicklung des technischen Teams (ca. 10 Mitarbeiter) mit Fokus auf Kompetenzaufbau, Motivation, Leistungsmanagement und Förderung einer integrativen One-Team-Kultur.
  • Einsatzplanung und Ressourcenmanagement inklusive Schichtplanung, Bereitschaftsdienste, Urlaubskoordination sowie Sicherstellung ausreichender Personalkapazitäten.
  • Koordination und Steuerung von Subunternehmern sowie enge Zusammenarbeit mit Soft-Service-Teams und Projektmanagern zur Gewährleistung reibungsloser Abläufe.
  • Technische Unterstützung bei Kapitalinvestitionsprojekten in Abstimmung mit Projektmanagern und dem Workplace Operations Leader.
  • Work-Order-Management und Digitalisierung: Koordination aller technischen Aktivitäten über das Ticketsystem mit vollständiger Dokumentation und Nachverfolgung.
  • Optimierung des Gebäudemanagementsystems (BMS) zur intelligenten Gebäudesteuerung unter Einbindung interner und externer Expertise.
  • Compliance und Risikomanagement: Sicherstellung der Einhaltung aller gesetzlichen, JLL-internen und kundenspezifischen Anforderungen zu Gesundheitsschutz, Arbeitssicherheit und Umweltschutz in Zusammenarbeit mit europäischen Fachverantwortlichen.
  • Durchführung und Koordination von Sachverständigenprüfungen, technischen Audits und gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Inspektionen (elektrische Anlagen, HVAC, Brandschutz).
  • KPI- und Performance-Monitoring: Tracking relevanter Kennzahlen, Erstellung von Reports und kontinuierliche Ableitung von Verbesserungsmaßnahmen.
  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Kosteneinsparungsinitiativen bei gleichzeitiger Aufrechterhaltung höchster Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsstandards
  • Innovationsmanagement: Identifikation und Implementierung neuer Technologien und Prozesse zur nachhaltigen Verbesserung der Servicequalität und Kundenzufriedenheit.
  • Budget- und Bestellmanagement in Abstimmung mit JLL-Prozessen, einschließlich Purchase-Order-Verwaltung und Kostenkontrolle.
  • Kundenorientierung und Serviceverantwortung: Sicherstellung exzellenter Kundenerfahrung und proaktive Kommunikation mit allen Stakeholdern zur Übertreffung der Serviceerwartungen.

Qualifikation

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Gebäudetechnik, Versorgungstechnik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder vergleichbar ODER Meister in der Haustechnik (HLS, Kälte-Klima)
  • Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im technischen Gebäudemanagement, idealerweise in komplexen Liegenschaften (Labore, Produktionsstätten, Innovation Centers)
  • Nachgewiesene Führungserfahrung mit technischen Teams
  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung und Koordination von Subunternehmern
  • Fundierte Kenntnisse in gebäudetechnischen Anlagen (HVAC, MSR/BMS, Sanitär, Brandschutz)
  • Sicherer Umgang mit CAFM- und Ticketsystemen sowie Work-Order-Management-Tools
  • Verständnis für Compliance-Anforderungen, Sachverständigenprüfungen und gesetzliche Vorschriften (BetrSichV, DGUV, etc.)
  • Kenntnisse in präventiver Instandhaltung und technischer Dokumentation
  • Erfahrung mit KPI-Tracking und Performance-Management
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
  • Sichere Englischkenntnisse für die Kommunikation mit Kunden und die Bedienung technischer Systeme
  • Ausgeprägte Führungs- und Coaching-Fähigkeiten
  • Hands-on-Mentalität mit gleichzeitiger strategischer Denkweise

Benefits

  • Attraktives Gehalt, Bonussytem
  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge
  • Gesundheitliche Zusatzleistungen
  • Umfassende Programme zur beruflichen Weiterbildung
  • .... und viele weitere Vorteile eines Großkonzerns

  • Gemeinsam mit uns einen neuen Social-Media-Account aufbauen
  • Kreative Videos für TikTok, Instagram Reels & Co. entwickeln
  • Malen-nach-Zahlen-Sets ausprobieren und den Prozess authentisch begleiten

  • Neue Content-Ideen und Formate entwickeln
  • Unsere Community für das kreative Hobby begeistern

Qualifikation

  • Du bist begeisterter Malen-nach-Zahlen-Fan
  • Du kennst dich mit Instagram, TikTok & Reels aus
  • Du hast ein gutes Gespür dafür, welcher Content unterhält und Aufmerksamkeit erzeugt
  • Du fühlst dich vor der Kamera wohl
  • Du kannst Videos mit dem Smartphone aufnehmen und idealerweise auch bearbeiten
  • Du bist kreativ, zuverlässig und bringst gerne eigene Ideen ein

Benefits

Du bekommst von uns die Produkte und alles, was du für deinen Content benötigst. Natürlich wird auch die komplette Zeit bezahlt, die du für das Malen der Bilder und die Content-Erstellung benötigst. Du malst also nicht in deiner Freizeit für uns, sondern das Malen ist Teil deiner bezahlten Arbeitszeit.

Dazu bekommst du viel kreativen Freiraum und die Möglichkeit, einen neuen Social-Media-Account von Anfang an mit uns aufzubauen und aktiv mitzugestalten.

Aever Clinics | München | Vollzeit oder Teilzeit

Du liebst Kosmetik, moderne Behandlungstechnologien und den persönlichen Kontakt mit Kund? Du möchtest hochwertige ästhetische Behandlungen durchführen, Menschen zu einem besseren Hautgefühl verhelfen und dich fachlich weiterentwickeln? Dann werde Teil unseres Teams bei Aever Clinics in München!

Über Aever Clinics

Aever Clinics gehört zu einer wachsenden europäischen Klinikgruppe im Bereich Beauty, Hautgesundheit und ästhetische Behandlungen. Wir verbinden moderne Technologien, hochwertige Behandlungen und eine persönliche Betreuung, um unseren Kund erstklassige Ergebnisse zu ermöglichen.

Für unseren Standort in München suchen wir eine engagierte und kundenorientierte Kosmetikerin oder einen engagierten Kosmetiker, die oder der unser Team verstärkt und gemeinsam mit uns wachsen möchte.

Deine Aufgaben

Beratung und Kundenbetreuung

· Du führst professionelle Beratungsgespräche sowie Haut- und Körperanalysen durch.

· Du verstehst die Wünsche und Bedürfnisse unserer Kund und berätst sie zu geeigneten Behandlungen.

· Du erklärst Behandlungsabläufe, mögliche Ergebnisse und die richtige Nachsorge verständlich und kompetent.

· Du baust durch deine freundliche Art und deine fachliche Kompetenz langfristige Kundenbeziehungen auf.

Durchführung von Behandlungen

· Du führst Laser-Haarentfernungen sowie weitere Haut-, Körper- und ästhetische Behandlungen entsprechend deiner Qualifikation und unserer angebotenen Leistungen durch.

· Du arbeitest nach unseren Behandlungsstandards, Protokollen und Sicherheitsvorgaben.

· Du sorgst für eine angenehme Behandlungsatmosphäre sowie für höchste Hygiene- und Qualitätsstandards.

· Du dokumentierst die Behandlungen sorgfältig und gibst deinen Kund passende Nachsorgeempfehlungen.

Qualität, Sicherheit und Geräte

· Du beachtest alle geltenden Sicherheits-, Hygiene- und Behandlungsrichtlinien.

· Du erkennst mögliche Kontraindikationen und klärst offene Fragen vor der Behandlung.

· Du setzt die Geräte fachgerecht und entsprechend deiner Schulungen ein.

· Du achtest auf die Einsatzbereitschaft der Behandlungsräume und Geräte und meldest technische Probleme zeitnah.

Kundenbindung und Teamarbeit

· Du sorgst für ein hochwertiges Kundenerlebnis vom ersten Beratungsgespräch bis zur Nachbetreuung.

· Du empfiehlst passende Behandlungspläne und Pakete auf Grundlage der individuellen Kundenbedürfnisse.

· Du trägst durch guten Service und kompetente Beratung zur Kundenzufriedenheit, Kundenbindung und zum Erfolg der Klinik bei.

· Du arbeitest eng mit dem Clinic Manager und dem gesamten Team zusammen und unterstützt einen reibungslosen Klinikalltag.

Das bringst du mit

· Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als staatlich anerkannte Kosmetiker oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation im Bereich Kosmetik, Hautpflege oder Ästhetik.

· Eine gültige NiSV-Fachkunde für die Anwendung nichtionisierender Strahlung zu kosmetischen Zwecken, insbesondere im Bereich optische Strahlung und Haarentfernung, ist erforderlich.

· Ein gültiger Lasersicherheitsschein ist erforderlich.

· Idealerweise praktische Erfahrung mit Laser-Haarentfernung sowie weiteren apparativen oder ästhetischen Behandlungen.

· Interesse an moderner Hautpflege, innovativen Behandlungstechnologien und ästhetischen Dienstleistungen.

    About us

    We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient.

    If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it.

    We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK.

    The role

    We're looking for a chemist who combines organic synthesis with strong analytical expertise. You'll synthesise biological molecules — including peptides, nucleic acid derivatives, and modified building blocks — and develop methods to understand how they behave in chemical and biochemical reactions.

    Analytical method development is a central part of the role. You'll use chromatography and mass spectrometry to identify products, quantify reaction progress, and resolve complex mixtures. Working closely with our enzymologists and computational scientists, you'll help decide what to make, how to measure it, and what the results tell us about the underlying chemistry.

    What you'll do

    • Design and execute syntheses of biological molecules and their derivatives, optimising reaction conditions and purification strategies.

    • Develop and troubleshoot LC-MS/MS methods, particularly triple-quadrupole methods for targeted quantification of substrates and products.

    • Apply Orbitrap-based proteomics workflows to characterise peptides, proteins, and their modifications.

    • Establish compound identity and purity using chromatography, NMR, and mass spectrometry.

    • Work with experimental and computational colleagues to design assays, test proposed chemistry, and investigate unexpected results.

    • Build reproducible synthetic and analytical workflows, with appropriate controls, calibration, and clear documentation.

    Essential experience

    We're interested in what you've made and measured, and how you approached the chemistry. We care about:

    • Practical experience in organic synthesis of biological molecules, particularly peptides and/or nucleic acid derivatives.

    • Strong analytical method development skills, including sample preparation, chromatographic separation, and quantitative mass spectrometry.

    • Hands-on experience with triple-quadrupole LC-MS/MS and Orbitrap-based proteomics.

    • The ability to independently troubleshoot synthetic and analytical problems, from poor reaction yields to ambiguous spectra or matrix effects.

    • Sound scientific judgement about experimental design, data quality, and what your measurements can support.

    Highly preferred

    • Experience with solid-phase peptide or oligonucleotide synthesis, bioconjugation, or non-canonical building blocks.

    • Familiarity with acoustic ejection technologies for sample handling or mass spectrometry.

    • Experience developing high-throughput analytical workflows or integrating methods with laboratory automation.

    • Experience characterising enzyme-catalysed reactions or working closely with chemical biologists and enzymologists.

    Logistics

    Compensation is highly competitive. We're also able to sponsor visas for the right candidate.

You understand failure modes, evaluation, cost and risk, not just architecture diagrams.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p>Data/AI balance</p> </td> <td> <p>Roughly 70/30, with demonstrable recent depth in AI (last 2–4 years), for example AI agents, AI advisory or AI foundations with large UK clients. Experience on NVIDIA and other modern tech stacks will be great addition<strong>.</strong></p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p>Commercial acumen</p> </td> <td> <p>Comfortable with P&L, business cases and ROI conversations, and able to negotiate with CFO-level stakeholders.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p>Leadership</p> </td> <td> <p>Experience leading and scaling teams of this size, in a matrix, through change.</p> </td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <br><br><strong>Location and travel</strong> <ul> <li>UK-wide remit. Through One WPP and the Elevate28 transformation agenda, we are building a simpler, more integrated, agile and AI-powered enterprise. WPP’s Performance & Culture Center of Excellence brings together the capabilities that help our people, teams and organisation perform, grow and thrive. Within it, Enterprise Effectiveness aligns WPP’s organisation, workforce and teams around its strategic priorities and enables the change required to deliver them.</p> <h1>About the Role</h1> <p>The Workforce Intelligence & Analytics Manager is a contract role that will build the evidence base for the workforce and organisation decisions that matter most to WPP. This role will turn fragmented people, organisation and business data into clear insight, forward-looking scenarios and practical recommendations that help leaders decide where to invest, how to shape the workforce and how to organise for performance.</p> <p>Reporting to the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, you will support the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence while working closely with business, People & Culture, Finance, Data and Technology partners. You will establish a trusted workforce-intelligence capability that supports strategic workforce planning and informs priority organisation, workforce, team and people decisions across Enterprise Effectiveness and the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence. This is not a traditional reporting role. It combines strategic analytics, internal consulting and leadership of a four-person data and reporting team based in India. You will be expected to work through ambiguity, connect disparate data and systems, and progressively turn fragmented analytics into a more integrated, trusted and usable capability. As a contract appointment, the initial focus will be to establish the core workforce-intelligence approach, strengthen the India-based team and deliver insight against WPP’s highest-priority workforce and organisation questions.</p> <h1>Why This Role Matters</h1> <p>WPP’s transformation requires faster, better choices about work, skills, capacity, organisation and investment. Those choices cannot be made from disconnected dashboards or backward-looking metrics alone. In this role, you will create a more integrated view of the workforce, translate evidence into choices and trade-offs, and help leaders anticipate the implications of AI, changing client demand and new ways of working. The work will directly shape how WPP builds the capabilities, capacity and organisation required for Elevate28.</p> <h1>What You’ll Do</h1> <h2>Build a trusted workforce intelligence capability</h2> <ul> <li>Working with the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, shape and build an enterprise workforce-intelligence approach that connects people, organisation and business data to the decisions leaders need to make.</li> <li>Define a focused set of workforce and organisational measures, dashboards and decision-support tools, moving reporting from activity and headcount toward capacity, capability, cost, productivity, risk and value.</li> <li>Partner with data owners and technology teams to map fragmented data and systems, define analytical requirements, and strengthen data definitions, quality, accessibility and responsible use, while being clear about limitations and the strength of the evidence.</li> <li>Establish repeatable analytical standards, governance and quality controls so insight is trusted, comparable and usable across WPP.</li> <li>Apply AI and automation to improve how workforce data is integrated, analysed and translated into decision support, while maintaining appropriate human judgement, transparency and responsible-use standards.</li> </ul> <h2>Enable strategic workforce planning</h2> <ul> <li>Help business and People & Culture leaders translate strategy, growth priorities and choices about how work is organised into workforce demand, capability and capacity requirements.</li> <li>Build scenarios that show the implications of different choices, including developing, hiring, accessing external capability, automating, augmenting, redeploying and exiting work or roles.</li> <li>Assess the current workforce and future talent supply, including critical skills, capacity, cost, location and role mix, highlighting gaps, risks and investment priorities.</li> <li>Connect workforce planning to business and financial planning cycles so decisions are timely, owned and grounded in common assumptions.</li> </ul> <h2>Deliver forward-looking insight and decision support</h2> <ul> <li>Use statistical analysis, forecasting and scenario modelling to identify emerging workforce and organisational risks, opportunities and patterns.</li> <li>Bring structure to ambiguous business questions, identify what can be answered with available data, test hypotheses and distinguish meaningful signals from correlation or noise.</li> <li>Turn analysis into clear choices, trade-offs and recommendations for senior leaders, including the consequences of action and inaction.</li> <li>Develop concise executive narratives and visualisations that make complex findings understandable without oversimplifying them.</li> </ul> <h2>Strengthen organisation and transformation decisions</h2> <ul> <li>Provide analytical support for organisation design, organisational health, inclusion and impact, talent development, team effectiveness and change priorities across Performance and Culture.</li> <li>Create baselines and evaluate whether organisation and workforce interventions are improving the intended outcomes.</li> <li>Combine quantitative evidence with qualitative insight to explain not only what is happening, but why it matters and where targeted action is needed.</li> <li>Identify enterprise patterns across businesses, markets and functions and convert them into practical recommendations for leaders and Enterprise Effectiveness partners.</li> </ul> <h2>Scale tools, capability and adoption</h2> <ul> <li>Build practical tools, templates and self-service products that improve the quality and consistency of workforce decisions.</li> <li>Coach People & Culture and business partners to interpret workforce insight, challenge assumptions and use scenarios in decision-making.</li> <li>Create a clear intake and prioritisation approach that focuses analytical capacity on the highest-value enterprise questions.</li> <li>Continuously improve the offer through user feedback, adoption evidence and emerging practice in workforce analytics, AI and organisational science.</li> <li>Lead and develop a four-person data and reporting team based in India, setting clear priorities, strengthening analytical and consulting capability, and shifting delivery from fragmented reporting toward higher-value workforce intelligence and decision support.</li> </ul> <h1>Minimum Qualifications</h1> <ul> <li>Relevant experience applying data and analytics in finance, commercial, operational or other business settings, together with experience in people analytics, workforce intelligence or strategic workforce planning.</li> <li>Experience translating business questions into analytical     About Orakl Oncology

    At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

    Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

    About the Role

    We are looking for an Alliance & Delivery Manager to own Orakl's pharma partnerships after signature: the partner relationship, the delivery of each research program, and the growth of each account.

    Orakl runs research programs for pharmaceutical companies on its virtual patient cohorts, combining compound screening, multi-omics and O-Predict analyses on the partner's assets. Several programs run in parallel on the same wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and the portfolio is growing. Delivery quality directly drives renewals and follow-on contracts.

    This is a high-ownership, partner-facing role. You are the partner's main contact, you are accountable for delivery across our wet-lab and dry-lab teams, and you grow existing accounts. You will also scale our delivery processes and tooling: project tracking, capacity planning and partner reporting, automated wherever possible.

    You will work closely with the Scientific Program & Operations Lead, Business Development, the Wet Lab, Data Science and Computational Biology leads, and Product. As the ideal candidate, you have already delivered complex scientific programs for pharma clients, and you are an expert at establishing partner trust.

    What You'll Do

    Own partner relationships: act as the main point of contact for each pharma partner from kick-off to final delivery. Map decision-makers, priorities and expectations for their asset, run the steering committees, attend key international conferences a few times per year and present results alongside our scientific teams.

    Lead program delivery: translate each signed contract into an executable plan for the Wet Lab and Dry Lab teams, with owners, milestones and deliverables. Own the timeline, coordinate the experimental and computational work, and ensure every deliverable passes internal QC and review before it reaches the partner.

    Manage capacity across programs: plan capacity with the Wet Lab and Dry Lab leads, arbitrate conflicts between programs and protect committed timelines. Centralise requests on delivery teams coming from partners and Business Development.

    Manage risk and change: anticipate delivery risks, including results that change the plan, and escalate to the Scientific Program & Operations Lead with a recommendation. Agree and document scope and timeline changes with partners.

    Scale delivery processes and tooling: scale our project management system in Asana, from program templates and timelines to portfolio and capacity views. Automate reporting and follow-up, deploy AI tools where they remove manual work, and document how we run programs.

    Grow existing accounts: identify, qualify and convert follow-on opportunities within existing partnerships. Work with Business Development on scoping, proposals and pricing, and provide a feasibility assessment before anything is committed.

    Plan scientific and BD materials: schedule conference and BD material cycles as part of the delivery plan, and coordinate partner approvals for any communication based on partnered programs.

    Minimum Qualifications

    • 4+ years in project management, alliance and/or account management, or partner delivery in biotech, pharma, a CRO or a techbio.

    • Master's degree in a scientific or engineering field. A PhD is a strong plus.

    • Demonstrated delivery of complex scientific programs: you have led multidisciplinary projects from plan to final deliverable, including when results reshaped the plan.

    • Pharma-facing experience: you have managed pharma stakeholders through steering committees, negative results and scope negotiations.

    • Commercial track record: you have identified and converted follow-on opportunities within existing accounts.

    • Hands-on systems building: you have designed project management systems and automated recurring workflows.

    • Working knowledge of oncology or molecular biology, sufficient to lead scientific discussions with our teams and partners.

    • Fluent in English

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience in precision oncology or at a pharma-facing CRO.

    • Familiarity with patient-derived tumor models, omics or drug screening.

    • Scripting (Python) or experience deploying automation and AI tools.

    • Experience working with SOWs and contracts.

    • Professional French.

    Who You Are

    • An owner: you take responsibility for outcomes across teams you do not manage, and you make explicit trade-offs when programs compete.

    • Scientifically fluent: you understand what a result means for the partner's asset before you plan around it.

    • Steady under pressure: you replan quickly if the data changes, and you deliver difficult news to partners clearly and early.

    • A builder: you treat every recurring manual task as something to standardise or automate.

    • Commercially minded: you recognise when a partner's needs extend beyond the signed scope and turn it into a proposal.

    Why Join Orakl

    • Own a portfolio of pharma partnerships. Represent Orakl from signature to final delivery, with direct access to partner decision-makers.

    • Work on distinctive science. Deliver programs built on virtual patients cohorts, functional drug screening & multi-omics.

    • Build the delivery model. Design how Orakl runs partnered programs as the portfolio scales.

    • Work across disciplines every day. Alongside the biologists, data scientists and computational biologists who generate the results.

    • Help shape the team. Define the delivery capabilities and future team needs as the partnership portfolio grows.

    Interview Process

    1. Hiring Manager Call: align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

    2. Technical Deep Dive: discuss a pharma program you delivered: the plan, the problems, how you managed the partner and the outcome.

    3. Delivery Case: using an anonymised, representative scenario, build a plan, triage issues and prepare a steering committee. Present it to the team.

    4. Reference Call: speak with one or two people who have seen you manage partners and deliver programs.

    About Us

    Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

    Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

    About the Role

    As an RF Engineer (GNSS) in the Hardware (Electronics) team, you will own the radionavigation architecture of our products. Our systems need high-precision navigation and robust connectivity in contested, complex environments, and you will be the expert responsible for the RF subsystems, from antenna design to integration and compliance. You will design custom GNSS antennas and receiver modules, extend them towards CRPAs for GNSS-denied operations, and see each design through simulation, lab validation and flight tests. Based in Lausanne, Switzerland.

    Responsibilities

    • Antenna Design: Design custom GNSS antennas and receiver modules for our products, and extend the work towards CRPAs (Controlled Reception Pattern Antennas) for GNSS-denied environments.

    • Antenna Integration: Integrate all antennas (GNSS, radio link) into the drones, validating through simulation (gain diagrams) and real-life lab and flight testing.

    • GNSS Test Bench: Develop, maintain and configure the GNSS test bench to simulate satellite constellations and interference scenarios.

    • RF Measurement: Run hands-on characterization with network and spectrum analyzers, and simulate new antenna iterations with EM software.

    • Electromagnetic Compatibility: Lead EMC troubleshooting and pre-compliance testing, identifying and removing blockers early.

    • PCB Collaboration: Work with PCB designers to review routing, shielding and RF layout.

    • Architecture Ownership: Review and own the RF architecture across product lines, including link budgets and system-level RF performance.

    • Mentoring: Act as the team's RF subject matter expert, coaching junior engineers on RF layout principles and EMC mitigation.

    Candidate Requirements

    • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, Telecommunications or a related field.

    • Experience: Proven track record taking complex wireless devices from concept to mass production, including clearing strict EMC compliance hurdles. Background in aerospace, commercial drones or GNSS products is a strong advantage.

    • GNSS: Solid grounding in GNSS, including hands-on use of a GNSS test bench to simulate edge-case environments, and an understanding of effects such as multipath.

    • Antenna Design: Experience designing custom antennas under tight mechanical and space constraints, with EM simulation tools.

    • RF & EMC: Strong command of RF fundamentals and measurement equipment (network and spectrum analyzers); comfortable working in an anechoic chamber.

    • Mindset: Analytical, meticulous, structured and resilient; a hands-on problem-solver who works autonomously and collaborates well.

    • Communication & Influence: Excellent written and verbal communication, capable of leading diverse principals, from junior members to senior executives.

    • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI's mission, vision, and ambitious growth plans, ready to go the extra mile to ensure operational excellence.

    We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

    At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

    As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

    This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

    Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

    What You'll Work On

    You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

    • Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events
    • Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them
    • Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading
    • Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise
    • Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible
    • Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales
    • Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models
    • Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper
    • Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems
    • Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

    No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

    What Success Looks Like

    Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

    Who We're Looking For

    We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

    • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

    Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

    Our Culture

    More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think.     At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The Role

CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.

These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:

  • They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.

  • They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.

  • They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

  • They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.

  • They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.

What you'll do

Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.

How we build

  • Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.

  • Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change.

  • Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters.

  • Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice.

Recent work

  • Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked.

  • A photo check for stray parts in robot storage scored 10 out of 10 blind, at about 8¢ a photo. The model it replaced caught about half.

  • Agent tool calls leave durable receipts, so a session killed mid-deploy resumes without sending the same email or order twice.

  • Invoices extracted from supplier emails matched what a person had entered 66 times out of 66.

  • A constraint solver replans the whole factory every two minutes, across robots, ovens and people.

What we look for

  • You've put LLM agents into production and can tell us what broke and how you knew it was working.

  • You're a strong software engineer first. Most of this job is real engineering, not prompting: concurrency, idempotency, data modelling, security.

  • You build the eval before you trust the result.

  • You like the physical world: cameras, robots, parts rotated by 90°.

  • Bonus: computer vision, optimisation or electronics.

Stack

  • Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Claude and OpenAI APIs, MCP, skills in plain Markdown

  • Code: TypeScript (Bun, React), Python (FastAPI, Dagster, OpenCV, OR-Tools), PostgreSQL

  • Infra: Nix and NixOS, Nomad, Terraform, Vault, AWS, Modal sandboxes, OpenTelemetry

Pay

About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The role
As a Senior Data Scientist for Product at Legora you will turn data into decisions. You'll sit close to the business, taking questions end-to-end: shaping the metric, modelling the data in dbt, running the analysis, and making the recommendation. You'll pull in new data sources when you need to. Insights are useful; impact is what we hire for.

We're an AI-first data team. We believe the data function should be redesigned around what AI now makes possible, not retrofitted with it, and we want someone excited to help define what that looks like in practice.

There's no single profile we hire for. Some of us are strongest at data modelling and analytics engineering, some at experimentation and causal inference, some at machine learning, some at stakeholder influence. You'll likely be excellent at one or two of these and competent across the rest. That's the bar.

We're a small, centralised team supporting the whole company, hiring for the person, not the seat. Depending on your strengths and where we have the biggest gap when you join, you could be embedded primarily with:

  • Product: instrumentation, feature adoption, user behaviour, A/B testing, shaping the roadmap with PMs and designers.

  • Finance & RevOps: ARR, NRR, forecasting, board reporting, pricing analytics across a 40-country footprint, and unit economics for an AI-native product.

  • Growth & Marketing: acquisition funnels, attribution, campaign measurement, lifecycle analytics, and what actually moves enterprise legal buyers.

  • GTM & Customer Success: pipeline analytics, customer health, expansion signals, and retention drivers in a category that didn't exist three years ago.

LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

    Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

    Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

    🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

    En tant que doctorant, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions de recherche et innovation et, dans une moindre mesure de nos missions d’enseignement. Vous serez affecté au centre SPIN – LGF (Laboratoire Georges Friedel, UMR CNRS 5307). Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal.

    Le centre SPIN (Science des Procédés Industriels et Naturels), qui sera fortement impliqué dans la thèse, développe, au sein de Mines Saint-Etienne, son expertise dans le domaine du Génie des Procédés appliqué aux systèmes dispersés : grains, particules, gouttes, bulles, milieux poreux. Il possède également des compétences en développement de capteurs et d’instrumentation.

    Les technologies de captage et stockage du CO2 sont des technologies clés pour la décarbonation du secteur industriel. Les stockages offshores ont déjà démontré leur faisabilité, mais les stockages onshores semblent nécessaires pour augmenter les capacités de stockage tout en réduisant le transport de CO2. Or, la proximité de ces sites avec les populations rend leurs déploiements incertains et soulève des questions relatives à l’acceptabilité sociale.

    La surveillance à long terme des sites de stockage de CO2, exigée par la directive européenne CCS, constitue une opportunité pour renforcer la transparence et l’acceptation locale du stockage en engageant les parties prenantes dans l’acquisition et l’interprétation des données. Cependant, les systèmes actuels de surveillance ne permettent pas à la fois de réaliser des mesures in-situ, simulations numériques et visualisation interactive pour une approche du suivi intégrée des sites de stockage. Le projet CO2MET vise à développer et faire progresser des unités ou éléments clés pour préparer un futur système intégré de surveillance numérique à long terme améliorant la fiabilité et l’acceptabilité du stockage géologique de CO2.

    Pour atteindre ces objectifs, le consortium CO2MET a été constitué et est composé de l'IFPEN, du BRGM, de Mines Saint-Etienne et de Cerema.

    La surveillance à long terme nécessite des outils fiables et performants, notamment dans le domaine des capteurs environnementaux, ce qui soulève la question de la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives pour traiter le signal, ainsi que celle de l'influence des variations à long terme des paramètres externes sur la réponse des capteurs (et de l'impact du changement climatique). Étant donné que les signaux de concentration en CO₂ peuvent, à eux seuls, ne pas être suffisamment discriminants (les concentrations biologiques dans les sols pouvant dépasser 10 % vol.), compte tenu de leurs origines diverses (sources profondes, provenant du stockage ou de l’interaction gaz-roche ; processus de respiration ; oxydation du méthane), la prévention des faux positifs dans la surveillance des sites de stockage doit s'appuyer sur des capteurs de CO₂ (NDIR ou photoacoustiques) et sur d'autres capteurs (par exemple, un capteur chimique d'O₂), ainsi que sur des capteurs environnementaux (humidité, pression, température) afin de permettre une attribution correcte de la source de CO2.

    Parmi les missions qui lui seront attribuées, le doctorant devra :

    · Sélectionner des capteurs existants répondants aux spécifications afin de mettre au point une plateforme de détection 

    · Etudier, en conditions de laboratoire, la sélectivité des capteurs vis-à-vis des espèces gazeuses interférentes, à l’aide d’une analyse multivariée

    · Définir des algorithmes de prédiction tenant compte de la reproductibilité, de la dérive, de la linéarité et de la variabilité dans des mélanges gazeux complexes et des conditions environnementales variables (température, pression et humidité relative)

    · Etudier l'influence du vieillissement des capteurs sur leur réponse et sur les prévisions établies, afin de proposer un algorithme de compensation

    ·  Enfin, mener des études de cas concrets sur le site de Sainte-Marguerite (Puy-de-Dôme), avec des niveaux d'émissions de CO₂ variables, afin de tester et de valider les plateformes de capteurs développées.

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now
  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

Trilogy Federal drives innovative solutions for complex business challenges across financial management, healthcare, and government industries. Our collaborative, client-first service approach, combined with our commitment to the rapid implementation of pragmatic solutions, has earned Trilogy an unparalleled reputation for delivering transformative results.

We are seeking an experienced Program Manager for a new part-time opportunity with an existing federal customer. The Program Manager will work closely with the client, the Program Partner, and subject matter experts to execute the program and will oversee all aspects of the Program.     • Develop and maintain project management documents including Project Management Plan, Project Schedule, Weekly Status Reports, Quality Assurance and Quality Control, among others.

    • Manage all work performed under the contract, overseeing the staff and the subject matter experts that support the program.

    • Develop documentation templates and protocols

    • Lead executive level meetings

    • Perform and oversee performance of accounting research

    • Develop presentations for client management

    • Develop policy and procedure templates and repository

    • Develop and oversee development of new or update accounting policies, procedures and process maps

    • Perform walk-through interviews of process owners

    • Design financial management dashboard(s) – identifying content and working with SMEs to develop.

    • Design presentation templates and graphic design tools and guidance

    • Develop training

    • Bachelors degree in Accounting

    • Minimum of 8 years of federal accounting or federal financial statement audit experience. 

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

    • The ability to obtain a Public Trust clearance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • CPA, CGFM or PMP is a plus.
